resolved_source_locations.conclusion: The structural laws of the Six Birds corpus through Foundations IV are stated from the standpoint of an external theorist: the theorist declares a lens, detects an obstruction, installs a repair, prices a residual, and runs the audit. This paper makes the closure apparatus part of the carrier. An endogenous closure system carries its own instruments, ledgers, repair generator, boundary records, and re-audit loop, and its claims of self-repair are admitted only when the relevant records are produced by its own transitions under a closed-loop source policy. Six definitions (D1–D6) and sixteen laws (E1–E16) give the resulting catalog: endogenous repair, bounded reflexivity, self-maintenance, repair compilation and collapse; priced exposure, alarm, control prices, and probe acquisition; stack rewrite, individuation, and repair transport; and reconsolidation, offline reclosure, and adaptability. The laws are carrier-side and substrate-independent. Living, cognitive, and social systems therefore enter on equal terms: physiological regulation and organismal maintenance, agent-side learning and control, and institutional reproduction and rewrite are distinct realizations of the same typed hypotheses, not metaphors for one another. Each law is stated in the six-part normal form inherited from Foundations IV, with an obstruction or falsifier, an exactly-one status partition where applicable, a proof spine, interaction discipline, and explicit nonclaims. D1–D6 and the core E1–E16 laws are represented in the companion Lean 4 development and finite Repair-World/law-specific campaign; two named interpretive corollaries, Alarm Fatigue and Operational Selfhood, remain unformalized and are marked accordingly. The finite campaign contains 348 preregistered comparisons across fifteen law-specific result artifacts, all passing. Existing particle and neural substrate experiments supply life-facing null, drive, maintenance, motif, and intervention evidence under explicit nonclaims, while an unrun planarian-regeneration protocol states a concrete biological promotion target and its falsifiers. No definition of biological life, consciousness, death, welfare, or autonomous evolution is claimed.

resolved_source_locations.conclusion: The anti-relabeling ledger is part of the result. This paper does not claim the predictive-state or causal-state quotient construction as new; that is a standard way to summarize a process by its predictive consequences . It does not claim the closure-deficit identity, or the optimality of the best autonomous macro-predictor, as new; those are imported from the closure-deficit and no-go accounts . It does not claim the strict-extension, saturation, or promotion-obligation framework as new; those are imported standards for recognizing when a higher vocabulary is a genuine layer rather than a relabeling . Nor does it claim as new the game-theoretic fact that added structure matters. Folk theorems show that repeated interaction can support many outcomes; global games show how noisy private information can select; reputation models show how type structure changes play; evolutionary and stochastic-stability models show that convention selection can be a property of a run; correlated equilibrium and type spaces show how signals and hidden state enlarge the game . These are reference points the paper uses, not results it rebrands. The contribution is the conjunction, on one explicit repeated-game object, under one evidentiary discipline. First, the paper installs the predictive state as the canonical institution of repeated play and verifies, on the finite carrier, that it is not definable from the game's own stage vocabulary: the institutional partition strictly refines the stage partition and does not factor through it. Second, the paper prices the omission exactly by closure deficit, with a gap–residual decomposition that separates what conditioning on the institution recovers from what remains unpredictable even after that conditioning. Third, it assembles these facts into a certified strict-extension object: the institutional vocabulary saturates, admits an active label-feedback exhibit under a declared extension, and passes the admissibility gates for a promoted layer on the carrier. Fourth, the picture is subjected to tests that could have failed silently but were reported in full: the run-layer constants are reproducible within protocol yet fail three frozen out-of-sample transfer attempts, and the human-data analysis confirms the predictive-residue hypothesis while reversing the proposed timing bridge. The registered negatives are not qualifications to the result; they are part of the evidence for the strict-extension reading.

resolved_source_locations.conclusion: We ask not merely whether layer birth occurs, but how many primitive kinds of birth are experimentally accessible. Within the Six-Birds framework, birth events can be organized by activation of packaging ( P5 ), directed circulation ( P6_ drive ), and staging anomaly ( P4 ). The strongest empirical separation is between Class-I and Class-II, where affinity at structural birth robustly discriminates drive-free from driven births and explicit no-fake-arrow controls rule out coarse-graining artifacts. We then place all four classes on a shared observable map using structural boundary location, affinity at boundary, and a strict-rule-aligned staging proxy. Capacity/depth behaves as a post-birth field rather than a primary classifier, and at least one upstream/PICA-style system can be embedded in the same coordinate system. We do not claim stabilized universality exponents. Instead, we provide a primitive taxonomy and observable separation of layer-birth classes that future universality work must respect.

resolved_source_locations.conclusion: Many sciences rely on maps of macroscopic behavior—phase diagrams, stability charts, bifurcation sets, and feasibility regions—but emergence itself is rarely treated as a mapping problem. We introduce emergence atlases: subsets and scalar fields on control space indicating where a macro-description is feasible. In the finite-state setting used here, feasibility means that a packaged description is simultaneously closed, nontrivial, audit-safe, and budget-feasible. We compute such atlases in three settings: analytic law families, full packaging spaces of small systems, and the PICA mechanism algebra. The resulting maps recover exact closure loci and reversible lines, expose multi-objective tradeoffs among closure, directionality, effective information, novelty slack, and budget, and identify mechanism-space regimes together with their sensitive ablations and conservative compact supports. These computations support a simple reframing: emergence is usefully treated as a phase-diagram problem for effective theories in control space. In that view, effective information, irreversibility, coarse-graining quality, and mechanism-space analyses appear not as rival definitions of emergence, but as slices of a larger atlas.
